tagline: Up the creek gorge, then over Briery Mountain.
intro: East of Morgantown, WV 7 winds beside Deckers Creek as the water turns from a gentle stream into a tumbling torrent through a narrow gorge, past limestone outcrops and overhanging rhododendron and laurel. Across the Cheat at Kingwood the road climbs Briery Mountain to 2,735 feet, and Terra Alta caps the mountain.

Between the two, the creek calms near Arthurdale, a New Deal homestead built in 1933 for unemployed miners and farmers. Eleanor Roosevelt took a personal hand in it, down to choosing the refrigerators for each house.

moments.title: Masontown
moments.text: Half a mile southwest of this town named for pioneer merchant William Mason, a row of 140 stone beehive coke ovens is built into the hillside above Deckers Creek.

moments.title: Arthurdale
moments.text: More than 100 of the homestead's original buildings still stand, along with a New Deal museum.

moments.title: Terra Alta
moments.text: After the climb up Briery Mountain, the town's Latin name, meaning high land, needs little explanation.
